nodes.name: Email queued?
nodes.notes:
A Code node has exactly one output, so Route Request cannot hand the mail branch its own item. Instead it returns one item and the `notify` payload rides along on it, absent when there is nothing to send.

This node is the gate that stands in for the missing second output: true (something was queued) goes on to "Which email?", false ends the branch. Without it every request would reach the Email nodes and `notify.to` would resolve to empty.

nodes.name: Which email?
nodes.notes:
Splits the mail branch on the `kind` that Route Request stamps onto every queued email.

kind = confirmation  ->  "Email: Confirmation"
everything else       ->  "Email: Reschedule"

Anything unrecognised deliberately falls through to the second branch, so a kind added to the workflow later still gets delivered instead of silently vanishing. Both nodes carry identical parameters today; keeping them separate means you can give one a different From name, reply-to address or template without touching the other.

nodes.name: Email: Confirmation
nodes.notes: Sent when the studio confirms a booking. Queued by Route Request on updateStatus -> confirmed.

nodes.name: Email: Reschedule
nodes.notes: Sent when the studio offers alternative times. Queued by Route Request on reschedule with payload.options.
